title: Outlook for iOS: PDF previewer opens sensitivity-label protected PDFs and adds a navigation toolbar
summary: The roadmap facts and PDF encryption command are supported, and targeted searches confirmed the feature-specific documentation gaps. The licensing model understates the published subscription requirements, and the briefing should acknowledge the Outlook FAQ's older statement that native attachment preview does not support rights management.

claims.claim: The Outlook for iOS PDF previewer now supports sensitivity-label protected PDFs.
claims.quote: MIP-label protected PDFs are now supported in the PDF previewer along with a built-in control's toolbar for easier navigation.
claims.fix: Add to What's changing: 'The Outlook for iOS and Android FAQ still says iOS native attachment preview does not support rights management and reports an error for rights-protected attachments; the roadmap now describes protected-PDF support.' claims.where: controls[0].ui and api; summary; Governance controls
claims.claim: No admin UI switch or API/app configuration key for Outlook for iOS PDF preview availability is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook iOS PDF preview disable admin app configuration PowerShell Graph attachment preview'. Read Outlook mobile app configuration settings and configuration-key tables, Exchange cmdlet reference and policy search excerpts; preview-blocking results concern Windows/OWA, not iOS.

claims.claim: No admin UI setting for EnablePdfEncryption is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'EnablePdfEncryption enable PDF attachment encryption admin center UI setting'. Read Message encryption FAQ, Set-IRMConfiguration reference and Automatically encrypt PDF documents with Exchange Online; each documents PowerShell, with no admin UI route found.

claims.claim: Set-IRMConfiguration -EnablePdfEncryption $true enables PDF attachment encryption using Microsoft Purview Message Encryption.
claims.quote: The EnablePdfEncryption parameter specifies whether to enable the encryption of PDF attachments using Microsoft Purview Message Encryption. Valid values are: - $true: Messages that contain PDF attachments can be encrypted.

claims.claim: The PDF attachment encryption setting has tenant scope.
claims.quote: Use the Set-IRMConfiguration cmdlet to configure Information Rights Management (IRM) features on your organization.

claims.claim: EnablePdfEncryption is available in Exchange Online, not on-premises Exchange.
claims.quote:
### -EnablePdfEncryption
Applicable: Exchange Online, Built-in security add-on for on-premises mailboxes
This parameter is available only in the cloud-based service.

claims.claim: Enabling PDF attachment encryption needs at least the Information Rights Management role.
claims.quote: To enable encryption for PDF attachments, using a work or school account that has the Information Rights Management role at a minimum in your tenant, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell:

claims.claim: A PDF automatically encrypted with the encrypted email inherits that email's permissions.
claims.quote: When Exchange Online uses Microsoft Purview Message Encryption, you can automatically encrypt PDF documents when they're attached to an encrypted email. The document inherits the same permissions as those for the email message.

claims.claim: The documented PDF encryption configuration concerns Message Encryption rather than PDF encryption inherited from a labelled message.
claims.quote: Outlook doesn't currently support PDF attachments inheriting encryption from a labeled message.

claims.claim: Exchange decrypts protected messages server-side before passing them to Outlook for iOS and Android.
claims.quote: Exchange decrypts any protected messages before passing them to the client. In other words, decryption is performed server-side.

claims.claim: The Outlook for iOS and Android FAQ says the app does not decrypt protected messages itself.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android doesn't perform any decryption itself.

claims.claim: The cited Outlook mobile app configuration keys include no PDF preview key or attachment key beyond the sync window.
